subject.title: [RFC] Multi-Agent Collaboration Enhancement: Capability Profiling + Shared Blackboard + Layered Memory + Token Cost Governance

question: Should #35203 remain the canonical broad multi-agent collaboration RFC, be split into narrower scoped core/API issues, or move the heavy orchestration pieces to plugin/ClawHub?
rationale: The RFC crosses core state storage, memory visibility, agent delegation/routing, config, cost governance, and security boundaries, while current VISION.md supports better agent harness capabilities but rejects heavy default orchestration in core for now.

options.title: Keep Canonical And Split First Slice
options.body: Keep #35203 open as the canonical direction, then ask maintainers to choose one narrow first implementation slice with storage, config, and security scope defined.

options.title: Narrow To One Phase
options.body: Convert this issue into a specific approved phase such as capability profiling or cost governance and track blackboard/memory/meeting work separately.

options.title: Move Heavy Orchestration Out Of Core
options.body: Route blackboard/orchestrator implementations to plugins or ClawHub and keep this issue only for missing plugin SDK or core security seams.

recommendation.title: Keep Canonical And Split First Slice
recommendation.body: Keep #35203 open as the canonical direction, then ask maintainers to choose one narrow first implementation slice with storage, config, and security scope defined.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest related scoping decisions in #65403, #64435, and #64392 and current history on central affected files.
